title: Cairn schema document, format version 1
description: A Cairn schema document defines the traits, entity types and relationship types of one origin. Write it as YAML 1.2 or as JSON. The same keys are used in both. A key that is left out takes its default: not required, not unique, not abstract, an association, not symmetric, not outliving its targets, not deprecated, no classification, and no supertype, traits, aliases, inverse aliases, constraints, examples, description, rules or checks. Anchors, aliases, explicit tags, merge keys, duplicate keys and several documents in one stream are not part of the format.

$schema.description: The location of the JSON Schema that describes this document, for editors that look for it. Cairn does not read it and does not write it.

cairn.description: The version of the document format. It must be the integer 1.

origin.description: The origin of the definitions: the name of the model and its version.

traits.description: The traits of the origin, by name. A trait declares attributes that entity types include.

entityTypes.description: The entity types of the origin, by name.

relationshipTypes.description: The relationship types of the origin, by name. The name of a relationship type is also the name of navigation from source to target.

origin.description: The name and the version of an origin.

name.description: The name of the origin, for example the name of the model.

version.description: The version of the origin. Always a string: write it in quotes, because a plain 1.10 is the number 1.1.

trait.description: A trait: attributes that entity types include. A trait cannot be a supertype or an end of a relationship type.

attributes.description: The attributes the trait declares, by name.

deprecated.description: True if the trait should no longer be used.

entityType.description: An entity type: concrete or abstract, with attributes, traits and at most one supertype.

abstract.description: True if entities cannot be of exactly this type, only of its subtypes.

supertype.description: The name of the supertype, which must be an entity type.

traits.description: The names of the traits whose attributes the entity type includes.

attributes.description: The attributes the entity type declares itself, by name.

aliases.description: Previous names of the entity type.

deprecated.description: True if the entity type should no longer be used.

rules.description: The rules that apply to the entity type and its subtypes.

checks.description: The checks that apply to the entity type and its subtypes: expressions over the values of one version of an entity, by name.

relationshipType.description: A relationship type from a source entity type to a target entity type.

source.description: The name of the source entity type.

target.description: The name of the target entity type.

targetsPerSource.description: How many targets each source can have: 0..1, 1..1, 0..* or 1..*.

sourcesPerTarget.description: How many sources each target can have: 0..1, 1..1, 0..* or 1..*.

inverseName.description: The name of navigation from target to source.

kind.description: A composition owns its targets: each target has exactly one source. An association does not.

symmetric.description: True if the two ends are interchangeable. Source and target must then be the same entity type, with the same multiplicity at both ends.

outlivesTarget.description: True if the relationships of the type may continue after their target ends, as records of a past fact: the target must exist where a relationship starts, and wherever it starts again after a gap in its effective period, and navigation then returns the target's last version. Only associations that are not symmetric can declare it, and subtypes do not inherit it.

supertype.description: The name of the supertype, which must be a relationship type.

attributes.description: The attributes the relationship type declares itself, by name.

aliases.description: Previous names of the relationship type.

deprecated.description: True if the relationship type should no longer be used.

rules.description: The rules that apply to the relationship type and its subtypes.

checks.description: The checks that apply to the relationship type and its subtypes: expressions over the values of one version of a relationship, by name.

attribute.description: An attribute: a value type, and constraints on the values. Ranges are for int, long, decimal, date and instant attributes. Allowed values, a pattern and lengths are for string attributes.

type.description: The kind of value the attribute holds. A date is ISO 8601 (2026-01-05). An instant is ISO 8601 with Z or an offset (2026-01-05T09:00:00Z); an offset other than UTC, such as +01:00, is converted to UTC.

required.description: True if every entity or relationship must have a value.

unique.description: True if no two entities may have the same value at the same time.

derived.description: A CEL expression that computes the attribute's value from the other values of the same version when a transaction commits, at most 4,000 characters. Read an attribute that is not derived as self.name, and test an optional one with has(self.name) before reading it; a derived attribute cannot read another derived attribute. Functions of Cairn's own count days between two dates: cairn.calendarDays(first, last) and cairn.workingDays(first, last) give the number of days from the first date to the last, as dates in UTC, both included, and workingDays counts only Monday to Friday. The result must fit the value type: a string for string, a bool for boolean, an int for int and long, a double for decimal, a timestamp for instant, and a timestamp at the start of a day in UTC for date; an optional attribute has no value if the expression gives null. A write cannot set a derived attribute. For example: self.givenName + ' ' + self.familyName.

range.description: The interval that values must lie in.

deprecated.description: True if the attribute should no longer be used.

classification.description: The classification of the attribute, such as pay: lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 128 characters. A reader or writer sees or sets the attribute's values only with a clearance that covers the classification; the attribute has no classification if the key is left out, and everyone reads it. A derived attribute that reads classified attributes must have the classification that they have.

examples.description: Typical values. Each must have the value type of the attribute and satisfy its constraints.

allowedValues.description: The values a string attribute may have. If the list is left out, any value is allowed.

pattern.description: A regular expression in I-Regexp (RFC 9485) that a string value must match as a whole.

minLength.description: The smallest length of a string value, counted in Unicode code points.

maxLength.description: The largest length of a string value, counted in Unicode code points.

range.description: The interval that values must lie in: at most one lower bound (atLeast or greaterThan) and at most one upper bound (atMost or lessThan). The bounds must have the value type of the attribute.

atLeast.description: The lower bound, included in the range.

greaterThan.description: The lower bound, excluded from the range.

atMost.description: The upper bound, included in the range.

lessThan.description: The upper bound, excluded from the range.

ruleReference.description: A reference to a rule that is written in Java, by name and version.

name.description: The name of the rule: lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

version.description: The version of the rule, a whole number.

attributes.description: A mapping from attribute names to attribute definitions.

checks.description: A mapping from check names to checks. A check name is lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 128 characters.

check.description: A check: an expression in the Common Expression Language (CEL) over self, the values of one version of an entity or relationship, that every version must make true.

expression.description: The CEL expression, at most 4,000 characters, whose result is a boolean. Read an attribute as self.name, and test an optional attribute with has(self.name) before reading it. Functions of Cairn's own count days between two dates: cairn.calendarDays(first, last) and cairn.workingDays(first, last) give the number of days from the first date to the last, as dates in UTC, both included, and workingDays counts only Monday to Friday. For example: self.lastDay >= self.firstDay.

message.description: What to tell whoever breaks the check. Without a message, the problem names the expression.

multiplicity.description: A minimum of 0 or 1 and a maximum of 1 or unbounded (*). Write it in quotes.

literal.description: A value of the attribute's value type: a number for int, long and decimal, true or false for boolean, and a string for string, date and instant.

int32.description: A whole number that fits 32 bits.
